entityDescription:
KRONO-SAFE is a privately-owned company founded in 2011 to commercialize software technologies originally developed with the French atomic energy commission (CEA). 
KRONO-SAFE develops and markets ASTERIOS, an integrated software tool-suite including an innovative real-time kernel (RTK) for safety-critical real-time embedded applications running on single- or multi-core hardware target platforms. 
KRONO-SAFE serves markets in need for a safer and more efficient solution to develop complex real-time embedded applications. These extend to both well-established markets such as aeronautics, space, defense, automotive, industrial automation, transportation, energy and new markets springing up where safety and security converge like the Industrial Internet of Things.
With a fifty-strong team of experts and a management staff of seasoned professionals, KRONO-SAFE is firmly focused on software development as a way of efficiently serving its customers. The company holds a portfolio of patents securing all its breakthrough solutions developed so far and is actively pursuing its innovation and patenting activities.

entityDescription: Omnisense is a privately owned micro-SME based near Cambridge, UK. The company has developed a versatile solution for high precision indoor and outdoor relative positioning, based around the ability to measure true time of arrival ranges between devices in unsynchronised radio sensor networks using COTS componentry. Our sophisticated Joint Timing and Location Engine can utilise all measurement inputs provided to it, which are based around both a 2.4 GHz and a UWB radio in the cluster relative positioning solution the company has developed. This is being targeted at key verticals we have identified in agriculture, maritime and construction, amongst others (including defence, mining, sport, healthcare). As well as the core location engine, system development has involved the development of full mobility mesh networking protocols, data management tools and a suite of APIs which make the business of providing applications to consume the positioning data easy for developers and integrators.

entityDescription:
One of the main causes of accidents both on the highway and in the mine is human error, often caused by fatigue resulting in drowsy driving, or sometimes poor driver behaviour. WOMBATT's mission is to eliminate fatigue as a cause of haul truck accidents in open pit mines, and to eliminate drowsy driving and poor driving behaviour as a cause of long distance truck and bus accidents on highways anywhere in the world, no matter how remote or inaccessible the route. 

By using the latest satellite and other communications methods, WOMBATT's skilled, locally recruited monitors can see all of the drivers all of the time, wherever they happen to be on the surface of the planet, Communicating in real time with drivers and fleet operations staff in their local language via two way communications satellites, WOMBATT monitors help keep drivers and those around them safe and alive, with a Spanish/English language fatigue monitoring centre in Lima, Peru, and an English/Afrikaans monitoring centre in South Africa.

As fatigue results from behavioural and organizational as well as physiological problems, WOMBATT conducts continuous, on site change management training, driver and supervisor training, and family training in the local communities in the local language. Fatigue training participants have full access to their own private page on the WOMBATT Online Training portal, where they can access all their own training materials as well as real time updated data on their sleep, fatigue and diet history.

Safe driving in the most remote and dangerous parts of the world requires real time monitoring by human beings, intervening immediately when things go wrong. Lives are saved by using the most advanced low cost satellite communications technologies that the Space industry and others can provide, combined with the best possible training at every level, delivered by world class fatigue, diet, sleep, human factors and change management professionals specifically for local people.

entityName: Lockheed Martin UK Strategic Systems Limited
entityDescription:
Lockheed Martin UK – Strategic Systems is the single contractor providing specialist Waterfront In-Service Support to the Royal Navy. 
LMUK SS, as part of the ABL Alliance with AWE and Babcock, are responsible for the management of operations at the Royal Naval Armaments Depot Coulport (RNAD(C)).
LMUK SS are currently engaged in Lockheed Martin Space activity in the UK as part of the UK Spaceflight Programme on behalf of the UK Space Agency under 2 separate Grant Agreements. Agreement 1 is for a UK Launch Pathfinder Project. The Project creates an initial UK launch capability by performing a pathfinder launch of a small launch vehicle. Agreement 2 is for an Orbital Manoeuvring Vehicle (OMV) Upper Stage Pathfinder. The project performs the research and development (R&D), build, and flight demonstration of an OMV, a smart upper stage specifically tailored for deploying constellations of small spacecraft, to create a new UK small launch service capability unique to the commercial space sector.

entityName: DLR - SPACE OPERATIONS AND ASTRONAUT TRAINING (DLR RB) Oberpfaffenhofen
entityDescription:
Competence and Innovation for the Way to Space!
DLR Space Operations is the central institution for spaceflight operations in Germany with locations in Cologne, Oberpfaffenhofen and Weilheim. This responsibility includes satellite missions for Earth observation, science and communication missions as well as for the exploration of the solar system and human spaceflight missions. Furthermore, astronauts are trained, space experiments are prepared and sounding rockets are developed and launched from sites around the world. Eventually, DLR works on new technologies, such as on-orbit-servicing in order to master even the most difficult space projects of the future.
In close cooperation with other DLR institutions and together with public and industrial partners, DLR Space Operations plays a major role for spaceflight in Europe. Here, groundbreaking space projects are realised and new ideas for spaceflight of tomorrow are developed. As a versatile interface between technology development, operations and utilisation, DLR Space Operations serves as an important venue for everyone involved in spaceflight and the general public. This is where groundbreaking projects are realised and new ideas for shaping the future of space flight are developed.

entityDescription: Furtwangen University (HFU), formerly the Fachhochschule Furtwangen (FHF), is a German University of applied science in Furtwangen im Schwarzwald, Baden-Württemberg, Germany. HFU was originally founded as a clockmaking school in 1850 by Robert Gerwig. The German Clock Museum, founded by Gerwig in 1852, remains a department of the university to this day. After World War II, the school was split into two branches: one for engineering and the other for job training. The engineering branch became a Fachhochschule when this type of university was introduced in the early 1970s. The Hochschule Furtwangen University has three campuses: Furtwangen (main campus), Villingen-Schwenningen and Tuttlingen.

TEKEVER ASDS (Aeronautics, Space, Defence and Security) was created in 2008 as a spin-off of the TEKEVER Group, and serves as the Group incubator for innovative technologies for the aerospace, defence and security markets. The company develops technologies up to maturity levels consistent with the creation of new ASDS products or the spin-off for integration into existing product lines of other companies of the Group. TEKEVER ASDS is completely privately owned and counts on highly skilled, experienced and motivated staff. 95% of the staff has undergraduate (BSc) or graduate (MSc) and post graduate (PhD) degrees and their backgrounds cover different disciplines, from Mechanical and Electronics to Aerospace, Software and Industrial Engineering. 
TEKEVER ASDS current areas of activity include:
Manned and Unmanned Aeronautics
Drones can mean anything from simple toys up to large aircraft capable of detecting stranded survivors in the middle of the ocean. Unmanned aircraft will have their place in society, be it at filming, ferrying cargo, monitoring the environment, or transporting people. By applying Agile development methodologies, TEKEVER is making flexible aircraft capable of fulfilling multiple roles and of providing access to airspace to everyone.

Satellites
Achieving economies of scale in the world of satellites is quite a challenge: Bringing innovation, standardisation, mass reduction and quick development together into a single package is a difficult nut to crack. Grouping these packages into networks is another ballgame. TEKEVER is working on pushing Nano and Pico Satellites further to achieve these goals. Small is the new Big!

Launchers
Getting into space is tough! Gravity is a drag and anytime you want to leave you need to take everything you need to survive for as long as you’re there, with you. What if you could send things into space as easily as taking a flight from Lisbon to Tokyo? TEKEVER is working towards delivering launch capability at a fraction of the cost for small payloads.
